reader.requirement: At --std 85 END-WRITE closes the scope of an indexed WRITE, so the statements after it are not part of its INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY phrases and a delimited WRITE can stand as an imperative inside another statement's conditional phrase, an IF arm or an inline PERFORM; an END-WRITE with no open WRITE is refused.

edition-consulted.switches: GateFilePhrase refuses WRITE FILE below 2002; GateRetryLockPlace places RETRY/LOCK (refused at 1985); END-WRITE itself is not gated

reader.edition-search: grep of END_WRITE in the grammar (one optional token closing writeStatement) and of Edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion around VisitWriteStatement; the scope is parse-tree structure, the same at every edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no (for END-WRITE; 1985 refuses the 2002 FILE phrase)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf02_07 covers the top level and an IF; not a delimited WRITE nested in another WRITE's or a READ's INVALID KEY, in an inline PERFORM, or a stray END-WRITE

probes.printed: D1 00 / INNER-WRITTEN / OUTER-INVALID-TAIL 00 / D2 / READ-INVALID-TAIL / LOOP-INVALID 1 / LOOP-TAIL 1 / LOOP-INVALID 2 / LOOP-TAIL 2 / W4-WRITTEN
probes.expected: each END-WRITE ends its own WRITE; the tails belong to the enclosing phrase, loop or IF

probes.printed: COBOL0306: unexpected 'END-WRITE'. END-WRITE appears without a matching WRITE statement.
probes.expected: refused: a scope terminator with no statement to end

probes.printed: COBOL0900: the FILE phrase of a WRITE or REWRITE statement requires COBOL-2002

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR10  (4.9.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR10
citations.quoted: The END-WRITE phrase delimits the scope of the WRITE statement

reader.notes: END-WRITE is the optional closing token of writeStatement and nesting falls out of the grammar. Every nested form ran as the scope rules require.

refuter.evidence: r10_nest.cob (r10_nest-001): a delimited WRITE with its own NOT INVALID KEY nested in an outer WRITE's INVALID KEY (O-INV 22 / I-NOTINV 00 / O-INV-TAIL, outer NOT INVALID not run); a delimited inner WRITE inside an outer NOT INVALID KEY, followed by a statement that stays in the outer phrase up to the period (outer INVALID taken: AFTER2-WRONG not printed, AFTER2-SENT printed); a delimited WRITE in a SEARCH WHEN (S-NOTINV 00 / S-TAIL); a doubly delimited WRITE in WRITE (INNER-AGAIN 22 / AFTER-DOUBLE). r10_after.cob (--compile-only, r10_after-001): a NOT INVALID KEY after END-WRITE refused with COBOL2269 (its text cites §2023:5.2.1 at --std 85, a label nit outside this rule). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR10  (4.9.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR10'.
